video.title: Bloomberg Tech Event Special | Bloomberg Tech 6/04/2026
video.display_title_html: Bloomberg Tech Special: The AI Capital-Formation Cycle

thesis: AI has shifted from a product cycle to one of the largest capital-formation cycles in history — splitting the market into capex-receivers (compute, energy, memory) and capex-spenders (the labs) — even as Broadcom's miss, a wave of trillion-dollar IPOs, and the Fed's still-absent productivity data show the boom is racing ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Mary Daly, San Francisco Fed President

insights.headline: Broadcom's $16B custom-silicon guide missed and erased $300B
insights.body: Broadcom guided to $16B of current-quarter custom silicon (TPUs/ASICs) revenue versus a Street expectation of $17.2B, triggering its worst drop since January 2025 — down as much as 15% and roughly $300B in market cap — after the stock had added $270B running into earnings.

insights.headline: 'The opposite of a bubble': demand outruns supply
insights.body: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman argued AI is the inverse of a bubble: builders are absurdly behind demand, with a backlog of more than $25B, and none of Cerebras, AMD, or Nvidia can keep up with what employees are driving.

insights.headline: AI's great divide: receiving capex vs spending it
insights.body: Altimeter's Apoorv Agarwal's central mental model splits AI into capex-receivers (compute, memory, optics, networking, energy — the 'picks and shovels') and capex-spenders (the labs). Knowing which side a business sits on is, he argues, the biggest divide in AI right now.

insights.headline: Databricks CEO: we already have AGI
insights.body: Ali Ghodsi says ~90% of any audience he polls agrees frontier models are smarter than most coworkers most of the time, so AGI has effectively arrived — the bottleneck isn't intelligence but missing context, which is what Databricks' Genie product aims to feed in.

insights.headline: Novo Nordisk cut trial analysis from weeks to minutes
insights.body: Ghodsi cites Novo Nordisk (maker of Ozempic) feeding all its clinical trials into Databricks' Genie, letting staff query obesity-study progress and compressing the time to understand studies from weeks down to a few minutes.

insights.headline: More software written in a year than all human history
insights.body: Ghodsi says Databricks calculated that within roughly one to two years more software will be written than in all of human history — driving demand for everything around software, including databases like Databricks' LakeBase, which is tailored for agents.

insights.headline: xAI/SpaceX as the 'Switzerland' of compute
insights.body: Agarwal frames SpaceX/xAI as taking a neutral 'Switzerland' approach — selling compute ('Elon Web Services'), models, a coding product and more — rather than betting on a single category, which is why he sees the addressable market (space plus AI) as so large.

insights.headline: Okta CEO: SaaSpocalypse is 'completely overblown'
insights.body: Todd McKinnon says fears of a SaaS apocalypse are overblown — like the cloud transition, laggards who don't embed agentic capabilities will become legacy vendors bought up by Oracle, but many will transition and thrive.

insights.headline: Okta will have far more engineers in five years
insights.body: McKinnon predicts Okta will have far more software engineers in five years — not despite efficiency gains but because there is so much more to build, so much demand for software, and so much automation leverage.

insights.headline: The bottleneck isn't models — it's connections
insights.body: McKinnon argues models already far surpass companies' ability to wire systems together into practical agentic apps; the barrier to agents that simply 'act' is secure connectivity to data sources, which is Okta's focus.

insights.headline: Fed: still no economy-wide AI productivity gains
insights.body: SF Fed President Mary Daly says despite above-trend US productivity, businesses have not reported transformative, ongoing AI gains yet — they say 'next year' is the litmus test, because the payoff requires transforming business processes, not just adopting a model.

insights.headline: Daly: a rising market isn't a financial-stability risk
insights.body: Daly notes most AI investment is funded by the MAG7 from their own resources; a market rise alone isn't a stability concern — that would require contagion into banks, consumers, or businesses, which she doesn't currently see.

insights.headline: Data-center inflation is a timing question
insights.body: Daly frames the data-center buildout as inflationary early (electricity demand, competition for scarce equipment and generators) but disinflationary later as the infrastructure and big-tech-funded power generation come online — currently oil and food, not AI, drive inflation.

insights.headline: Bad year to IPO; markets are too busy
insights.body: Ghodsi says Databricks will eventually go public — driven by the need to create a liquidity mechanism for ~14,000 current and former employees after raising ~$20B — but calls this 'a terrible year to go public' given how much is happening at once.

action_items: Classify any AI bet by whether it receives capex (compute, energy, memory, networking) or spends it (the labs) — Agarwal's framework is the clearest lens on where durable value accrues.
Stop waiting for smarter models and start capturing context — Ghodsi argues the gap between today's agents and useful autonomy is missing data context, not model capability.
Treat 'next year' as the AI productivity litmus test — Daly says economy-wide gains require transforming business processes, not just deploying a model.
